case_name: Jasleen Kaur Sidhu vs Shikhar Kacker
facts_of_case: The parties got acquainted in 2010 and married in 2014. The wife sought interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act. The trial court partly allowed her application. The husband appeals against the order.

legal_principles.principle: The court may order the respondent to pay expenses of proceeding and monthly sum during the proceeding if it appears that either party has no independent income sufficient for their support.
legal_principles.held: Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support...

legal_principles.principle: The court should dispose of the application for payment of expenses and monthly sum within sixty days from the date of service of notice.
legal_principles.held: Provided that the application for the payment of the expenses of the proceeding and such monthly sum during the proceeding, shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within sixty days from the date of service of notice...

outcome.final_order: The final court order enhanced the amount of maintenance granted to the wife.
